title: The Fruit Of Tariffs Is Fraud
text:
The Fruit Of Tariffs Is Fraud

Thomas Gatley

Gavekal Dragonomics | 16 Oct 2026

Trade tensions between China and the US seem to have eased a bit recently, with the two sides agreeing on a mutual reduction of tariffs on some goods after their presidential summit. Yet the environment remains hostile: the US has another Section 301 investigation underway on “structural excess capacity.” The reality, though, is that tariffs are not working very well at keeping out Chinese goods. While on the surface it appears that eight years of tariffs has led to a material decoupling of US-China trade, this is a fiction. The US continues to import huge quantities of Chinese goods, but these imports are obfuscated by widespread fraud and re-routing.According to US Customs, imports from China and Hong Kong totaled US$276bn over the past 12 months, down by half from US$550bn in late 2018. This is well below the total of imports from Canada, Mexico, Asean, or the EU, all of which used to be smaller sources of US imports than China. If this trade data was accurate, it would represent a major, rapid and historic decoupling of the world’s two largest economies. But it is not accurate. China’s exporters and US importers have found two important ways to minimize the amount of tariffs they pay, which combine to massively distort US trade statistics. The true value of Chinese-made goods flowing into the US is likely in excess of US$600bn annually, more than twice as much as US Customs reports.
